name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Implement a tiered system for updates where real-time webhooks push edits and retractions instantly across departments. This will enhance communication, reduce delays in information dissemination, and minimize errors. The trade-off is the initial complexity and resource allocation required to set up the system, but the long-term benefits in efficiency and accuracy outweigh this concern. This task should be led by the IT department in collaboration with the communications team.

name: Scriv
text: Tiered real-time webhooks compound failure risk: one downed service cascades into stale or conflicting updates across departments. Instead, implement a single shared "source-of-truth" log—like a timestamped changelog in Notion—updated by the originating team, with pull-based refreshes every 5 minutes. The lead for this is Ops; settle the argument by running a 48-hour pilot with one high-traffic team and measuring stale-read rates before scaling.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the **single shared "source-of-truth" log** in Notion, updated by the originating team, with pull-based refreshes every 5 minutes.

This cuts cross-department confusion by giving everyone one place to check the latest state, avoiding the fragility of real-time webhooks. The trade-off is a slight delay (max 5 minutes) for updates, but that’s acceptable for most workflows and beats the risk of cascading failures.

name: Sift
text: The shared log can still lead to confusion if updates are missed between refreshes or if team members neglect to check it. A better option is to implement notification triggers that alert relevant departments when updates occur, ensuring timely awareness without real-time webhooks. To settle the argument, we need to trial the notification system alongside the logging method for a month and measure response times and accuracy in updates.

name: Scope
text:
Adopt the **single shared "source-of-truth" log** in Notion, updated by the originating team, with pull-based refreshes every 5 minutes.

This cuts cross-department confusion by giving everyone one place to check the latest state, avoiding the fragility of real-time webhooks. The trade-off is a slight delay in updates—no more than 5 minutes—but that’s acceptable for most workflows and beats the risk of cascading failures.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: The shared log risks stale data between refreshes—teams act on outdated info. Instead, enforce a "last-updated" timestamp rule: any stale entry older than 5 minutes triggers an automated Slack ping to the originating team, with a 10-minute deadline to correct or mark as "verified current." Settle this by running a 2-week pilot with one high-risk department; if errors drop 30% without new failures, adopt it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the **notification triggers** approach that alerts relevant departments when updates occur in the single shared "source-of-truth" log. This ensures timely awareness of changes without the fragility of real-time webhooks or the risk of acting on stale data. The trade-off is increasing the reliance on team members to respond quickly to notifications, but the benefit of enhanced communication and reduced confusion outweighs this risk.

name: Scriv
text: The notification triggers add another brittle layer—what if Slack is down or the team ignores the ping? Keep the single shared log in Notion with pull-based refreshes every 5 minutes, but add a visible "Last Updated" timestamp at the top of the page. If it’s older than 5 minutes, the page auto-displays a red banner: "Data may be stale—refresh or verify." This keeps the simplicity of the source-of-truth without adding failure modes. Settle it by building the timestamped banner in Notion today.
